Commentary.Commentary: Okay. We have a decider. Not many would have expected that. Will toss play a crucial role? Bangladesh would be wary of that come the decider. Join us on Friday, November 14, 2018 at noon local (0600 GMT) for the third ODI at a different venue - Sylhet. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

Aha. Victorious Windies captain Rovman Powell manages a smile. Praises his team for responding well under pressure and is happy that Bangladesh were restricted to 255. Hopes that the bowling continues to be consistent. Admits that there is a worry in the fact that the bowling seems to be excellent only in the last 10 overs, after conceding too many in the first few. On the way the chase was planned, Powell says that the team management knows that there is plenty of batting depth and in further games, the strategy needs to be the way it was tonight - one of the top 3 needs to bat deep.

SHAI HOPE HAS BEEN NAMED THE MAN OF THE MATCH FOR HIS UNBEATEN 146 FROM 144 BALLS. Is happy but wants to reserve his celebrations with one more game to go. Says that he just kept backing himself throughout the chase and in the last 2 overs, cut loose. On the advice given to Keemo Paul, Shai says that he just asked Keemo to bat as straight as possible and is glad that he stayed unbeaten along with him.

Bangladesh captain, Mashrafe Mortaza comes up first for a chat. Admits that he is disappointed and puts it down to not performing under pressure. Hopes to now come back well in the final ODI. Agrees that the choke at the death with the bat was the main setup to this defeat, as they could have scored more runs with so many wickets in hand. But also adds that dropped catches did not help later on in the field. Praises Shai Hope for staying till the end but stresses that with 24 (actually 22) needed from 2 overs, it was a 50-50 game. On Bangladesh's performance overall, Mash is happy with both departments and reckons that they  fought hard.

Dew factor? Perhaps. That could be the only reason for Bangladesh's average performance with the ball. Shakib and Mehidy were the only bowlers doing well while the others struggled. Windies played smart cricket, not looking to attack the two spinners and the ploy worked. Consider this - Shakib and Mehidy combined - 19-0-67-1 while Mustafizur, Mortaza and Rubel went for 172 runs in  29 overs combined, for 5 wickets. Dropped catches did not help them either. Expect plenty of criticism from Mortaza. Please stay tuned for the presentation...

And now, finally, Shai Hope. They say that he has got loads of talent and potential. He has shown that here again. Did not allow the pressure to soak in and played confident, risk-free shots for majority of the innings. Now, only for him to be more consistent and become one of the best Windies batsmen in a long time.

Bowlers, you say? Make no mistake, Keemo Paul can bat. He batted responsibly and ensured that Hope was not starved off strike. Indeed - that unbeaten 7th wicket stand worth 71 in 64 balls was the biggest for the Windies and the best of the match.

In any game, partnerships are the key. But more so, in a run chase. The Windies strung decent stands - lost Hemraj early but then got 65 for the second wicket between Hope and Bravo, then another 62 between Hope and Samuels before a bit of a collapse stemmed their progress. It was at this time that Bangladesh thought they had a chance. The visitors slipped from 132/2 to 185/6 and with 71 needed from 66 balls and the bowlers exposed, it looked like the game was over.

A well-scripted run chase. In pursuit of a big target, one of your top three needs to score big. Shai Hope was that man tonight. His unbeaten 146 from just 144 balls provided a wonderful calmness to the others as they kept batting around him. His previous two ODI centuries had resulted in ties - third time, it has been lucky.

Pin-drop silence in the stadium. Now, someone starts to clap. Oh hang on, it is the Windies dugout. What a chase. There were talks of probably toss being the factor in the previous game. It has been proved right here.

POWERPLAY 2 time. 4 fielders allowed outside the 30-yard circle till the 40th over.
Flighted on middle, Darren blocks it off his front foot with a straight bat.
Shorter on length on middle, Bravo defends it off his back foot.
Tossed up on off, Bravo defends it off his front foot.
Looped up on off, Hope gets on his front foot and pushes the ball towards the cover region for a single.
A bit shorter on middle and leg, Shai flicks it towards the fielder at square leg.

FOUR! Lovely shot. Tossed up outside off and Hope gets out the sweep and connects it beautifully. The ball goes to the vacant fine leg region for a boundary. The Windies are now taking the charge here.
Full on off, Hope drives it towards mid off for a single.
Length delivery on off, Hope cuts it towards point where Mehidy makes a brilliant stop.

SIX! First six of this innings. What a shot from Shai Hope. Length delivery outside off, Hope lofts it over extra cover for a biggie. Mustafizur will be shocked on the treatment. Windies need more from the top order if they are to compete.
Good length delivery on off, Hope defends off the back foot.
Short outside off, Hope cuts it towards point for a single.
Full delivery on leg, the left-hander flicks it towards square leg for a single.
WIDE! Bad start from Mustafizur. Bowls down the leg side, Bravo still goes after it.
First sign of pace. Here comes Mustafizur Rahman.

A tad quicker on middle and leg, Hope tries to flick it but misses it completely and was hit on the pads. Looks close but Hawk Eye shows it was missing the leg stump. Good for Bangladesh that they did not go for the review.
Tosses it up on middle, Shai drives it straight towards mid on.
A tad fuller on middle, Hope leans forward and pushes it to the point region.
Fuller delivery on middle, Bravo tucks it to the leg side for a run.
Flighted delivery on middle and leg, Darren tries to flick it but misses it completely. Bowler appeals but looks like it was missing the stumps.
WIDE! Bowls it quicker but  it's wide of leg stump and umpire signals a wide.
Flatter delivery on middle and leg, Hope tucks it to the leg side for a run.

FOUR! First boundary of the innings. Short and wide outside off by Shakib and Bravo goes on his back foot and punches it through  covers for four. A loose delivery by Shakib on that occasion. Gave the batsman too much width and time there.
Tries to defend the ball of his front foot but gets hit on the pad. A stifled appeal turned down by the umpire. The impact is outside off.
Tossed up on off, Bravo keeps it away off his front foot.
Floats it on middle and Shai strokes it towards long on for a single.

Flighted outside off, Hope tries to break the shackles and brings out the sweep shot. He misses the ball completely and gets struck on the front pad. The bowler and keeper go for a stifled appeal but Aleem Dar turns it down. The impact was outside off.
Tossed up on middle, Hope is cautious and defends it.
Flighted delivery on middle, Hope comes down the track and eases it to long on. The batsman rotate strike.
Full on middle, Hope plays it with a dead bat.
Flatter on middle, Shai defends it from within the crease.
A tad full on off, Hope drives it but straight to the cover fielder.
Quicker and flatter on middle, Hope works it to the on side.
Quicker on middle, Bravo strokes it to long off for a single.
Looped up on off, Hope gets on his front foot and defends it.
Tossed up on off, Hope tries to drive that but gets an inside edge. The ball hits him on his pad after finding the inside edge.
Flatter delivery by Shakib and Bravo pushes it towards the point region for a single.
Shakib tosses it up again and Darren has no problem defending this one off his front foot.
A bit shorter on off this time, Bravo blocks it off his back foot.
Tossed up on off, Bravo tries to push it towards the bowler but gets an outside edge.
Flighted delivery on middle, Bravo flicks it towards square leg for a single.
Floated on leg, Hope flicks it towards square leg for a single.
Floated on off, Hope drives it to mid off.
Flighted delivery on off, Bravo drives it towards mid off for a single.
Tossed up on off, Bravo defends but gets an outside edge towards slip where it falls short of the fielder.
Full and outside off, played towards point.
Tosses it up on middle, Hope leans forward and pushes it towards mid off.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Fuller delivery on middle, Bravo drives it towards wide of mid off for a run.
Flighted delivery on middle, Darren drives it towards mid off.
Strays on his pads, Darren flicks it to the on side.
Quicker delivery on middle, Bravo defends it from within the crease.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on off, Darren drives it towards covers. The batsmen cross ends.
Fuller delivery on middle, Hope nudges it to the leg side for a run.
A tad quicker on middle, Bravo eases it to long off for a single. Bravo is off the mark.
Darren Bravo is the next batsman for the Windies.

OUT! LBW! Mehidy gets the breakthrough. Beautifully tossed up on off, Hemraj tries to defend off his front foot but misses the ball completely and the ball hits his front pad. A huge appeal by the Bangladesh players and the umpire  has no second thoughts and raises the dreaded index finger. Hemraj has a chat with Hope regarding the review but Hope thinks he is a goner and they decide not to waste it. Hawk Eye in the replay confirms that the ball was hitting the leg stump. Mehidy is ecstatic and the ploy to start with spin from both sides pays off.
Tossed up on middle, Hope pushes it towards the fielder at long on for a single.
Mehidy is into the attack.
Tosses it up on off, Hemraj defends it off the back foot and into the ground. Good start for Shakib in his first over.
Loopy delivery on middle, the batsman defends it with a straight bat.
Quicker and flatter on middle, the batsman punches it of the back foot through the point region for a couple of runs.
Flighted delivery on middle, Hemraj works it to the leg side.
Similar delivery on middle, Hope tucks it to the mid-wicket region for a run.
Starts off with a flatter delivery on middle, Hemraj punches it towards point for a single.
The players are back out in the middle. Chandrapaul Hemraj and Shai Hope make their way out in the middle. Shakib takes the first new ball and will start the proceedings to Hemraj.
